disqualifyingIssues: Heavy reliance on unfilmable narrator VO for internal states and plot
Major compression and invented soft dialogue with Thornton that flattens the rescue and love arc
evaluations.rationale: Covers main beats but leans on continuous narrator to carry emotion and exposition; many scenes pack multiple actions and lack camera-specific staging for 5-10s clips. Character looks are thin and dialogue often generic.

Tight, faithful compression of the novel into observable action beats ideal for short AI clips. Distinct visual locks on Buck and key humans; dialogue is sparse and period-true. Sound design is only lightly implied rather than prompted per scene.

Highest fidelity with locked Buck identity note and near-complete beat coverage including Dave’s death, the thousand-pound pull, and Ghost Dog coda. Action lines are concrete though some montages slightly overload a single heading; music/sound beds under-specified.
Excellent show-don’t-tell staging of fights, theft, and the ice collapse. Characters remain visually consistent; pacing serves clip length. Sound remains mostly implicit.

Extremely complete adaptation including Black Burton and the rapids rescue. Directibility is strong but density of incident in later reels risks multi-action scenes; still production-viable with minor splitting.
Faithful and dialogue-rich, yet several sequences cram location/action changes that would need splitting for 5-10s AI clips. Character intros are adequate but less rigorously re-locked than top tier.

Collapses entire novel into a vague short
No usable character visual locks or clip-scale structure
evaluations.rationale: Essentially a different, severely truncated story. Unusable as an adaptation of the source.

disqualifyingIssues: Invented named characters (Elias Holt, Edward Blake, Arthur Pike, Samuel Keene, Chief Kitchi, Warrior Makwa) constitute major source deviation
evaluations.rationale: Strong visual staging and clip-friendly action, but the closed-cast / fidelity violation from numerous invented proper names is a deal-breaker for a strict book adaptation.

Best overall package: locked Buck description, exhaustive yet clip-scalable beats, authentic dialect, and clean scene isolation. Sound design still only lightly indicated but every other dimension is production-ready.

judgeSummaryNotes: Strongest: Screenplay I because it delivers the fullest faithful beat coverage with locked character visuals and cleanly isolated, camera-ready actions ideal for 5-10s AI clips. Weakest: Screenplay G because it abandons the source plot, invents characters, and collapses the novel into an unusable short outline.
